newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- MURDOCH UNVEILS DIGITAL TV DEAL WITH US GROUP

News Corp Chairman Rupert Murdoch has announced a tie up between his company's digital satellite television service ASkyB, due to be launched in the US later this year, and EchoStar Communications of Denver. Under the trade name Sky the venture will provide more than 500 channels of digital satellite television along with a range of information services. The deal will also increase pressure on the US cable industry whose leading operator Tele-Communications Inc. lost 70,000 subscribers in the final quarter of last year.

97% of members of the UK's largest building society voted in favour of its conversion to a bank. The conversion still has to be approved by the Building Societies Commission but this is unlikely to be a problem and it will result in the Halifax becoming one of the UK's top twenty companies and the fifth biggest bank in the country. A market capitalization of up to 13 billion stg is expected when the company is listed on the stock exchange in June.
-- CLUB AIMS TO DRIVE DOWN COST OF SOLAR ENERGY

A global 'purchasing club' has been organised by a former campaigner with the environmental group Greenpeace, with the aim of driving down the costs of solar energy by persuading companies and local authorities around the world to invest in photovoltaic panels. The first UK company to sign up to the initiative, which is being 'marketed' on the basis that global warming and associated freak weather is a threat to the business of banks and insurance companies, is the insurer Guardian Royal Exchange. The scheme will be formally launched in June.
-- LANG PREDICTS MAJOR CHANGES TO ENERGY INDUSTRY

Trade and industry secretary Ian Lang has predicted that Britain's gas and electricity industries will undergo further restructuring as a result of the introduction of full competition planned for next year. In a speech delivered on his behalf on Monday night, Lang revealed that he expects more new entrants to the energy industry, including large retailing groups, and that more multi-utilities would emerge. He also dismissed rumours that the introduction of full liberalization of the domestic electricity market, planned for next year, would be delayed.
-- LIB DEMS TO OPPOSE WINDFALL LEVY

The Liberal Democrat party has said it will oppose Labour's planned windfall tax on the privatized utilities should Labour win the next general election. Announcing the party's own tax proposals, Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesman Malcolm Bruce said that they regard Labour's planned levy as a bad precedent that would not meet the need to increase training for the unemployed. The move will intensify the stakes in possible post-election bargaining between the Lib Dems and Labour.

Cambridge Combinatorial, a new company specialising in combinatorial chemisty, is to be launched on Tuesday. Biotech company Oxford Molecular will have a stake in the new company which is to be run by their Chief Executive Tony Marchington's younger brother Allan. Combinatorial chemistry is a technique for producing drugs designs and the company may form links with Pfizer, the UK's biggest US owned drug research and development company, where Allan Marchington was previously a research scientist.
-- UK PLANTS TO BENEFIT FROM VALEO REFORMS

French automotive components manufactuer Valeo SA has announced plans to strengthen its presence in the UK as part of reforms aimed at improving efficiency and driving down costs. The move is expected to benefit the group's plants in south Wales and at Blyth, north east England, which produces security systems and anti-theft devices. Valeo currently operates about 70 European plants, but the FFr3 billion (320 million stg) restructuring will leave it with fewer but larger plants.
-- MIXED START FOR HANSON AND ENERGY

Shares in Energy Group, the demerged former Hanson division, rose 43.5p to 568.5p on Monday, their first day of trading. By contrast, shares in the rump Hanson group - which now contains just building materials and equipment interests - edged up just 1.5p to 281.5p. Energy's closing price valued the new group at 3.6 billion stg, whereas Hanson's market valuation of 1.83 billion stg has prompted speculation it will soon be replaced in the FT-SE 100 index. -- PPL SHARES CLIMB AS DOLLY SAYS HELLO

Shares in biotechnology company PPL Therapeutics rose 52.5p to 387.5p on Monday following the announcement of a breakthrough in the company's patented technology for creating clones from the cells of adult animals. PPL, in conjunction with the Edinburgh- based Roslin Institute, announced the breakthrough at the weekend after producing Dolly, the first clone of a large adult mammal. Full details of the company's research will be published in this week's Nature magazine. -- MAID SELLS INTERNET SERVICE

Shares in the on-line service Maid rose 36p to 198.5p on Monday following news that the company has sold its Internet- based services to hotels to Fourth Communications Network. Under the deal, Maid will receive 10 per cent of 4th Network Internet access revenue for 30 years, with a guarantee of at least 11 million stg in the first three years. Maid will also take a 10 per cent stake in 4th Network. BMC +44-171-377-1742
